name: Bolivia
snapshot: The first non-MAS president in two decades scrapped fuel subsidies and turned to the IMF to stop an economic collapse that left queues at petrol stations.
culture: Bolivia has the largest Indigenous share of any South American country, with Quechua and Aymara the biggest groups, and 37 official languages. Cholitas, Aymara women in bowler hats and layered skirts, have reclaimed a once-derided style and even appear as wrestlers in El Alto. The Oruro Carnival and its Diablada devil dance are UNESCO-listed.
society: Under Evo Morales, the first Indigenous president, gas revenues cut poverty sharply. As gas output fell, dollars ran out, fuel imports dried up and inflation rose. Bolivia holds some of the world's largest lithium deposits. Coca leaf, chewed and drunk as tea, is legal and culturally central.
situation: In 2006, Evo Morales became Bolivia's first Indigenous president and used the proceeds of a natural gas boom to cut poverty sharply. One policy outlived the boom: fuel subsidies that froze petrol and diesel prices at 2006 levels for two decades. When the gas ran low, the state paid for imported fuel with its dollar reserves until they ran out. By 2025 Bolivia faced fuel queues, a black-market dollar and its worst economic crisis in 40 years, and voters ended almost 20 years of socialist rule by electing centre-right economist Rodrigo Paz.

In December 2025 Paz scrapped the subsidies by decree and sought a $3.3 billion IMF loan (Al Jazeera). Prices jumped, and cheap imported fuel damaged engines, enraging transport workers. From early May, unions, miners, coca growers and Indigenous groups, many allied with Morales, blockaded the roads into La Paz for weeks, cutting off food, fuel and medicine; demands snowballed into calls for Paz to resign. He cut his own and his ministers' salaries by half and fired his labour minister (Edition.mv/AFP). Nothing worked, and on 20 June, after 50 days, he declared a state of emergency so the army could clear blockades (Reuters via Aaj). A deal with the main union federation followed, but in September coca growers in Morales's Chapare heartland marched again over a diesel price rise. Morales, under an arrest warrant in a case he calls persecution, says Paz's government "doesn't have much of a future" (AFP via Kuwait Times). His former ally and successor, Luis Arce, is in custody over alleged misconduct as economy minister.
power: A presidential republic and "plurinational state" recognising 36 Indigenous nations. The president is directly elected for five years; the Plurinational Legislative Assembly has two chambers. Unions and social movements wield street power that has toppled presidents before.
